text: Zeno's ___ paradox argues that at every instant a moving projectile occupies a space exactly equal to itself and is thus at rest; if time is composed of such instants, it never moves.
explanation: This is the Arrow paradox, which targets the composition of time out of durationless instants: if the projectile is at rest at every instant and time is made of instants, it never moves. Aristotle replies that the now is a limit rather than a part, so time is not simply composed of instants. (The Dichotomy and Achilles, by contrast, exploit infinite divisibility rather than the instant.)
